text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak returned to Cairo from a one-week visit to Germany. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri met him at the airport.
- The Damascus Declaration states agreed to support Egypt's efforts to save the peace and set up an Arab common market.

- A front-page commentary noted that Thursday was the second anniversary of the attempt to assassinate President Mubarak in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa, an operation attributed to militant Islamists helped by Sudan. Al-Ahram said: "Egypt will not cease to hunt down the cowardly terrrorists until it uproots them and cuts off the hands of those who gave them support, help and shelter."

- It has been decided to offer 900,000 shares in Misr International Bank/MIBank on the New York stock exchange later this year in the form of global depositary receipts (GDRs). Ownership of the shares was transferred to the depositary bank yesterday.
- Military Production Minister Mohamed el-Ghamrawi said that next year the value of production by military factories will be two billion pounds ($590 million).
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will report to Mubarak on the Damascus Declaration meeting. Moussa said the meeting was successful and useful and there were no disagreements.
- The ministerial committee on privatisation will discuss at its next meeting a report on the timetable for selling 50 companies between July 1 and thre end of the year.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said there was no going back on implementation of the new law on relations between landlords and tenants of agricultural land. "We will not permit any attempt to stir up trouble," he said.
- U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said in Washington that the United States was giving priority to Egypt's efforts to save the Middle East peace process.

- Abdelhamid Ibrahim, the chairman of the Capital Market Authority, denied that Arab investors had pulled out of the Egyptian stock market. He said that transactions by Arabs were worth five billion pounds between March 1996 and May 1997, half of it in the first six months of this year.
- The MIBank GDR offer was covered more than six times over. Essam el-Ahmadi, the chairman of Banque Misr, said that demand was for shares worth $800 million.
